answer: Because the zenith record is per identity, the tundra audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. Promotion out of probation calls for 16 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, since every alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's dune standing. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
